1.name: Base
1.note: The cast foot. Its drillings link the pump, the reservoir and the ram chamber, and its valve pockets hold the balls.

2.name: Ram cylinder
2.note: The honed tube the ram slides in. The oil pressure acts on the ram's Ø32 head inside it.

3.name: Reservoir tube
3.note: The outer tube. The space between it and the cylinder is the oil reservoir.

4.name: Top nut
4.note: Closes the top of the tubes and guides the ram. It is the end stop at full lift.

5.name: Ram
5.note: The large piston that lifts the load. Oil pushes on its Ø32 head, so the large area gives the force multiplication.

6.name: U-cup seal
6.note: Seals the ram head to the cylinder. Pressure presses its lip tighter against the wall.

7.name: Wiper
7.note: Wipes the ram clean as it goes back down, so dirt stays out of the seal.

8.name: Extension screw
8.note: Screws out of the ram to adjust the starting height.

9.name: Saddle
9.note: The serrated cap that takes the load, so the load cannot slip sideways.

10.name: Filler plug
10.note: A rubber plug in the reservoir. It is how oil is topped up.

11.name: O-ring
11.note: Seals the ram cylinder to the base, so pressure oil cannot leak into the reservoir.

12.name: Pump cylinder
12.note: The small bore the plunger works in, and the lug the handle's link hangs from.

13.name: Oil
13.note: The working fluid. It is practically incompressible, so every cubic centimetre pushed in by the plunger moves the ram.

14.name: Pump plunger
14.note: The small piston. Each 25 mm stroke pushes a fixed volume of oil toward the ram, and its small area is the other half of the area ratio.

15.name: O-ring + back-up
15.note: Seals the plunger in the pump cylinder. The PTFE ring stops the rubber being pushed into the gap under pressure.

16.name: Link
16.note: Hangs the handle socket from the pump cylinder. It lets the socket swing as a lever.

17.name: Handle socket
17.note: The lever's short arm. It drives the plunger, and the handle's long arm multiplies your force again.

18.name: Handle
18.note: The long lever arm you push on. It gives the first multiplication, ahead of the hydraulic one.

19.name: Clevis pin
19.note: The pivots of the link, the fulcrum and the plunger.

20.name: Suction ball
20.note: The inlet valve. On the upstroke it lifts and lets oil be drawn in from the reservoir. On the downstroke it seats.

21.name: Delivery ball
21.note: The outlet valve. It opens on the downstroke to pass oil to the ram and closes on the upstroke so the load stays up.

22.name: Delivery seat
22.note: The brass seat the delivery ball seals on.

23.name: Delivery spring
23.note: Holds the delivery ball gently on its seat between strokes.

24.name: Relief ball
24.note: Lifts when the pump pressure passes the set limit and lets oil back to the reservoir, so the jack cannot be over-pressurised.

25.name: Relief spring
25.note: Its force sets the pressure at which the relief ball lifts.

26.name: Set screw
26.note: Retains the relief spring. The Ø2 hole lets the relieved oil pass.

27.name: Release screw
27.note: A needle valve back to the reservoir. Opening it lets the load drive oil out, so the ram sinks.

28.name: O-ring
28.note: Seals the release screw so oil does not leak past its thread when it is shut.

29.name: Expander plug
29.note: Plugs the ends of drilled oil passages in the base.
